name: The Kimball household at 1801 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_kimball_william_w

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1801 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1801 Mr. & Mrs. W. W. Kimball.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1801, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The seven live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: William W. Kimball

occupation.note: Founder of the W. W. Kimball Company, pianos and reed organs.

persons.note: He 'died at his home in Chicago on December 16, 1904' (Wikipedia), five months after the scene date. The 1900 census lists Wm. W. Kimball here as head, born May 1828, in Maine, married, piano mfg. (ED 40, sheet 3A, line 11, leaf n798).

persons.name: Evalyne M. Kimball
persons.note: The Blue Book prints her as Mrs. W. W. Kimball; Wikipedia names her Evalyne M. Cove, married to him in 1865. It names no children. The 1900 census lists Evaline M. Kimball here as wife, born April 1835 (the figures are hard to read), in Illinois (as read), married (ED 40, sheet 3A, line 12, leaf n798).

born.note: The census gives August 1871, age 28 on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (steward); born August 1871 (the figures are hard to read), in Canada (Eng.), came to the United States in 1893, single.
